goals: Make the exact Matcha Flavoured 1.12 server-data tree automatically available during Minecraft 26.2 Fabric create-world preparation and normal world reloads.
Preserve all existing Matcha namespaces, identifiers, source bytes, and server-data behavior without moving its client resource-pack assets.
scope: Package only the exact source pack.mcmeta and 2,433 files from the Matcha 1.12 data/ tree as one Fabric built-in server-data pack.
Register the pack as ALWAYS_ENABLED without globally reordering other packs, preserving the existing Matcha Vanilla Village Restoration module's explicit higher-priority village restoration.
Statically verify byte identity, all original namespaces and minecraft overrides, Frost Protection and Ribbits contracts, packaged-JAR contents, and exact-legacy-pack coexistence semantics.

exclusions: Any Matcha data rewrite, namespace rename, recipe/effect/loot/advancement/worldgen rebalance, Java recreation, or alteration of the immutable originals archive.
Matcha client assets, textures, models, sounds, UI, and any replacement for the existing Matcha client resource pack.
Automatic editing of worlds or automatic removal/disablement of legacy world datapacks.
Changes to Matcha Frost Protection, Matcha Death Rebalance, Matcha JEI Integration, Matcha Vanilla Village Restoration, Matcha Noxious Redstone, Ribbits, either runtime profile, or test-slot state.

dependencies.reason: The exact game target of the source pack and Fabric mod.
Minimum Fabric Loader declared by the built mod.
Provides the built-in server-data-pack registration API.
Immutable source of every embedded server-data file and pack metadata.
Its deliberate explicit priority remains the authority for the five restored vanilla village definitions.

state.milestone: Canary 1 embeds the exact Matcha Flavoured 1.12 server data as the ALWAYS_ENABLED Fabric built-in pack matcha_flavoured_data:matcha_flavoured_1_12. Static source/tree/JAR checks pass; both Test Slots are occupied, so no runtime profile or deployment was touched and runtime acceptance remains required.
